collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager dreamed a turtle told them to plant sweet roots by the big stone: plant them there, or laugh it off.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Last night (subject) dreamed that a large, serious turtle swam up to (subject.him/her) and said, very clearly, "Plant the sweet roots by the big stone." Then it swam away. (subject) has never planted sweet roots in (subject.his/her) life. (subject.He/she) tells (friend) about it over breakfast.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Well," says (friend), "it couldn't hurt." (subject) plants sweet roots by the big stone. They grow. Not spectacularly, but they grow. Was the turtle right? Was it just a dream? Would they have grown anywhere? (subject) doesn't know, and (friend) refuses to have an opinion. (subject) keeps an eye out for turtles after that.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "It was a dream," says (subject). "Turtles don't talk." "Not out loud, anyway," says (friend). (subject) doesn't plant the roots. A month later, (subject.he/she) notices a few wild sweet roots already growing by the big stone, all on their own. (subject.He/she) stares at them for a long time. It means nothing. Probably.
